synopsis: The booklet recommends response-surface methodology for fine tuning a handful of smooth, continuous parameters, including warning-distance offsets, persistence times, confidence thresholds and filter constants [f6673, f14425, f6965]. After influential factors have been identified, response-surface designs model curvature in a smaller subspace and provide interpretable main effects, interactions and local optimum regions under model assumptions [f6802, f6966, f7221]. The glossary reinforces its use for tuning thresholds and zones, while Chapter 9 also recommends response-surface and D-optimal DOE for constrained physical design spaces [f14104, f7220]. These methods are poor for discontinuous behaviour and cannot establish global corner-case coverage or operational probabilities [f7223, f7222]. Although response surfaces are mature, non-automotive-specific statistical techniques with an independent evidence base, the booklet reports no off-road evidence or published off-road braking application; applicability remains conditional on the stated assumptions being respected [f7398, f7226, f14429, f7399].
